analysis: The PR adds a single documentation row in docs/provider/cli-reference.md (head line 1751) describing the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP environment variable. It is mapped to ModelCalibrationPolicy.shapeWarmupEnvironmentKey; `0` disables the load-time shape warmup and `always` skips its shader-cache probe. No executable code, auth, attestation, key handling, wire protocol, or cache storage logic changes. Threat model relevance is limited: T-041 (prefix-cache TTFT oracle) concerns time-to-first-token; a load-time warmup toggle could change latency characteristics, but nothing here changes cache scoping, TTL, HMAC names, or encryption, and no evidence shows the variable affects cache hit/miss timing. The patch excerpt is complete and shows only this one-line addition. The base text units cover the surrounding CLI reference and show no security-relevant contradiction. Remaining integration question: the variable's implementation (ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift) is outside the supplied evidence, so whether the variable is forwarded into launchd and whether it affects behavior beyond warmup is unverified. Since the row is in an environment-forwarding table, whether it is actually forwarded cannot be confirmed from this docs-only change. No finding qualifies.
